questions.prompt: Which book by Jeffrey Gray does Peterson single out as exceptionally important for emotion and brain function?
choices: A Beyond Freedom and Dignity.
B The Neuropsychology of Anxiety (1982).
C Man and His Symbols.
D Thinking, Fast and Slow.
questions.explain: He highlights Gray's 1982 Neuropsychology of Anxiety on emotional response and brain function.

questions.prompt: What does a rat's runway pulling/running illustrate about motivation and incentive?
choices: A Motivation is imaginary and cannot be measured.
B You can index how much an animal wants something; approach toward reward underpins incentive reward.
C Rats only respond to punishment, never reward.
D Hunger never affects behavior once food is visible.
questions.explain: The rat is happy running toward food—incentive reward while moving toward the goal; satiation changes the frame.

questions.prompt: What critique does he level at the self-esteem movement in schools?
choices: A It perfectly eliminated all neurosis.
B It made kids more neurotic/higher in negative emotion and confused self-esteem with competence.
C It should replace all grades with stickers only.
D It proved that praise without standards always builds mastery.
questions.explain: Educational psychologists' self-esteem push made kids more neurotic and confused self-esteem with real competence.

questions.prompt: How does he suggest using fear productively rather than being stopped by it?
choices: A Ignore fear completely and never analyze risk.
B Let ordered fear propel you—know what to fear (including your own self-destructive stupidity).
C Maximize panic until you freeze permanently.
D Outsource all fear management to social media.
questions.explain: If fear stops you, you're stopped; if fear propels you, you're harder to interfere with—know what to fear.

questions.prompt: In exposure/daydream work, why does making a frightening fantasy more realistic help?
choices: A It proves the fantasy is false and can be ignored.
B More realistic fantasies (e.g., measured by sweating) speed progress in exposure therapy.
C Fantasy should always stay vague to protect the ego.
D Only group hypnosis works for fear.
questions.explain: More realistic frightening fantasies produce stronger physiological response and faster exposure progress.
